one_line: AI workspace that analyzes project changes and prepares reviewable replanning proposals.
what_it_does: Recomputes affected tasks, conflicts, alternatives, and budget adjustments when a project constraint changes, leaving approval to a person.
leverage_rationale: Structured agent assistance is useful for impact analysis over a shared plan, but the packet does not establish that a general UI-driving agent could not achieve the same outcome with friction.
leverage_evidence: About text describes agent analysis of a $50,000-to-$40,000 budget change and a generated change proposal.
Human review and approve/reject boundary is explicit.
execution_rationale: The described workflow is coherent and the screenshot packaging indicates an adaptive workspace, but no video frames or end-to-end runtime evidence are supplied.
execution_evidence: Demo is marked alive and gallery_images=5.
No video frame sheets submitted; description includes dashboard and change-proposal states.
impact_rationale: Project and operations teams have a concrete recurring need to understand downstream effects of changing constraints; the proposed reviewable workflow addresses it credibly, though demonstrated scope is limited.
impact_evidence: Specific budget-change scenario with affected tasks, conflicts, and alternatives.
Human approval preserves accountable decision-making.
creativity_rationale: Constraint-aware replanning with agent-prepared proposals is a useful new angle on project planning, but remains a recognizable productivity pattern.
creativity_evidence: Agent analyzes change rather than merely answering plan questions.
Proposal-and-human-approval interaction is clearly articulated.
usability_note: The stated flow is understandable, but visual and runtime usability evidence is thin.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame evidence.
About text is truncated in the packet.
advance_reason: Promising concept but insufficient packet evidence for advancement against stronger demonstrated projects.

one_line: Neuroinclusive water-cycle learning experience whose interface adapts to each learner.
what_it_does: Lets a browser agent adjust density, text, color, motion, audio, and response channels while preserving the learning objective and requiring human confirmation before submission.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes many precise, coordinated accessibility adaptations available through a shared interface state; this is materially more reliable than manually driving a complex LMS UI.
leverage_evidence: Five imperative WebMCP tools are described for real-time interface adaptation.
Agent can prepare an answer and open review but cannot submit academic work automatically.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a focused, coherent educational prototype with a concrete learner narrative and multiple adaptation dimensions; absence of video transcript and failed image access limits certainty.
execution_evidence: Deployed client-side HTML/CSS/JavaScript proof of concept on Vercel.
Description specifies Leo, Luma, Ayu, water-cycle lesson, and review boundary.
impact_rationale: Neurodivergent learners face a real mismatch between academic goals and rigid interface demands; adapting the path while keeping the goal fixed is a strong, credible fit.
impact_evidence: Specific audience and barriers: overload, dense instructions, motion, time pressure, and response constraints.
Supports voice, text, and visual participation.
creativity_rationale: The character-led, neuroinclusive learning model combines adaptive presentation and agent-mediated interaction in a notably thoughtful way.
creativity_evidence: Luma and Ayu frame a water-cycle lesson as a calmer adaptive experience.
Safety-aware answer preparation without autonomous academic submission.
usability_note: The stated controls target common accessibility pain points, though usability cannot be fully checked from unavailable frames.
red_flags: Frame sheets were listed but could not be inspected in this environment.
advance_reason: High-impact, well-scoped adaptive learning concept with substantial WebMCP leverage.

one_line: Multiplayer semantic whiteboard where humans and AI agents create together live.
what_it_does: Agents map codebases, create diagrams or artwork, inspect semantic canvas structure, and revise it alongside human collaborators in real time.
leverage_rationale: The core experience depends on agents sharing live semantic canvas state with humans and making inspectable, reversible edits; generic UI driving is substantially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Every canvas object has identity, geometry, relationships, revisions, and attribution.
Agents create, inspect, detect readability problems, and correct work on the shared board.
execution_rationale: The product scope, collaboration model, and semantic data model are unusually coherent, with real-time synchronization and research harness claims; visual verification was unavailable.
execution_evidence: Public repository and alive demo are reported.
Description names real-time multiplayer synchronization, Redis, Vercel, and efficient transactions.
impact_rationale: Remote teams, developers, designers, and agents have a real need for shared visual thinking; the product directly improves collaborative diagramming and ideation.
impact_evidence: Targets architecture diagrams, codebase mapping, illustration, and remote teamwork.
Mobile controls and shared live canvas broaden practical use.
creativity_rationale: A live semantic canvas with agents as visible co-creators is a memorable interaction model pursued beyond a conventional whiteboard.
creativity_evidence: Human and AI agents edit the same board together.
Visual trace, semantic inspection, and readability correction are distinctive behaviors.
usability_note: Live shared editing and mobile navigation suggest strong usability ambition; detailed frame inspection was unavailable.
red_flags: Frame sheets were listed but could not be inspected in this environment.
standouts: Agent work is visible rather than hidden.
advance_reason: Distinctive and highly WebMCP-native collaborative canvas with credible scope.

one_line: Evidence-backed workbench for auditing ML experiment comparability before approving next steps.
what_it_does: Imports bounded research records, reconstructs provenance, runs deterministic comparability checks, and supports human approval without granting the agent durable authority.
leverage_rationale: Structured access to bounded evidence, provenance, findings, and approval state makes agent-assisted research auditing precise and reviewable; a generic agent would face meaningful friction.
leverage_evidence: WebMCP-capable agent collaborates with deterministic audit rules.
Evidence package digest, citations, and explicit durable-authority boundary are central.
execution_rationale: The 141-second demo and detailed description support a complete, coherent workflow with explicit mismatch handling, provenance, and approval states.
execution_evidence: Video is submitted and transcript shows prepared examples, findings, and bounded authority.
Deterministic checks cover candidate pools, splits, preprocessing, metrics, and missing/conflicting evidence.
impact_rationale: Researchers and ML teams have a concrete high-cost problem: invalid comparisons can waste compute and misdirect conclusions. This directly addresses evidence quality.
impact_evidence: Specific failure mode of candidate-pool/evaluation mismatch.
Keeps metrics visible and avoids unsupported causal claims.
creativity_rationale: The combination of experiment-comparison auditing, canonical evidence packaging, and agent collaboration is an original and ambitious research workflow.
creativity_evidence: Confidence bounded by least-confident decision-relevant finding.
Recorded manifests take priority over declared configuration.
usability_note: Review-first findings and citations are well suited to careful research workflows.
standouts: Clear separation of agent prose from durable research evidence.
advance_reason: Excellent demonstrated execution and unusually rigorous research-assurance workflow.

one_line: WebMCP workflow studio for agents to fill and validate complex forms before human review.
what_it_does: Guides multi-step provisioning, lease, vendor-onboarding, and synthetic visa workflows, visibly validating required fields and producing a local receipt after confirmation.
leverage_rationale: Structured tools improve completion and validation of complex forms, but the same broad outcome remains possible through UI automation with real friction.
leverage_evidence: Five tested tools with visible UI effects are described.
Agent prepares grouped answers while a person retains final confirmation.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a coherent multi-workflow product with visible validation, review, and receipt states, supported by a deployed public repository and gallery evidence.
execution_evidence: Public repo and alive demo reported.
Gallery captions identify completed review, blocked required fields, architecture, and employee provisioning journey.
impact_rationale: Complex forms are a widespread operational pain point for employees, vendors, tenants, and administrators; accountable preparation can reduce errors and time.
impact_evidence: Concrete employee provisioning use case plus lease and vendor onboarding.
Required-field validation and human review directly address risk.
creativity_rationale: A practical synthesis of agent form completion, workflow validation, and accountable receipts; original enough in interaction but within a known category.
creativity_evidence: Grouped answer review before receipt creation.
Synthetic travel-visa sandbox is clearly labeled.
usability_note: Visible progress, validation blocking, grouped review, and receipts suggest a usable workflow model.
red_flags: No video transcript; evidence is primarily captions and description.
standouts: Human accountability is built into the form workflow.
Multiple concrete domains without disguising the synthetic sandbox.
advance_reason: Strong practical product with clear workflow evidence and credible audience value.

one_line: Assurance harness that independently verifies whether WebMCP actions changed real business state.
what_it_does: Separates tool claims from authoritative observations, evaluates them against human-frozen contracts, and creates tamper-evident replayable regression cases.
leverage_rationale: The product directly addresses the gap between structured WebMCP success claims and real outcomes; independent observers and replayable contracts are not a comparable generic UI-driving convenience.
leverage_evidence: Transcript demonstrates a successful discount response paired with an incorrect observed cart total and a failed verdict.
Uses Shopify cart endpoint observation and content-addressed replay cases.
execution_rationale: The 181-second video transcript provides unusually strong end-to-end evidence across local fixtures, repeated trials, human-frozen manifests, and a Shopify development store.
execution_evidence: Video shows discovery, catalog search, add-to-cart, false-success detection, restoration, and replay.
Transcript reports three bounded outcome trials with committed rows and correct failure classification.
impact_rationale: Silent success is a serious reliability and trust problem for any agent-operated workflow; this gives developers and evaluators a concrete assurance mechanism.
impact_evidence: Explicit distinction between call-level evaluator pass and failed observed business outcome.
Works against a real Shopify development store without admin access.
creativity_rationale: The dual-channel claim-versus-observed-outcome model and deterministic replay framing are highly original and deeply pursued.
creativity_evidence: Human-defined outcome contracts and content-addressed regression cases.
Explicit non-pass when authoritative evidence is unavailable.
usability_note: The evidence matrix and plain-language mismatch verdicts make a technical assurance workflow understandable.
red_flags: Demo is marked alive=unknown, though video evidence is strong.
standouts: Excellent separation of claims and observed truth.
Real external-store validation plus deterministic replay.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage, impact, creativity, and end-to-end evidence.

one_line: MODE lets users reshape website presentation through natural-language agent preferences.
what_it_does: Adapts a dense storefront’s layout, typography, content density, promotions, imagery, and sorting while preserving site-owned facts and functionality.
leverage_rationale: A structured preference layer lets an agent make coordinated, repeatable presentation changes that would otherwise require extensions, custom CSS, or brittle UI driving.
leverage_evidence: MODE exposes intentional developer capabilities for user-described presentation changes.
Preferences persist in cookies and distinguish site-owned facts from user-owned experience.
execution_rationale: The concept and demo packaging describe a focused storefront transformation with a clear principle and multiple adaptation controls; no transcript is provided.
execution_evidence: Public repo and alive demo reported.
Ten gallery images and three listed frame sheets support visual product evidence, though unavailable for inspection.
impact_rationale: Users with low vision, ADHD, price sensitivity, or strong presentation preferences have clear needs that conventional site controls do not fully address.
impact_evidence: Specific adaptations include larger text, stronger contrast, removing distractions, hiding images, and sorting products.
Preserves trusted site content and functionality.
creativity_rationale: Natural-language personal presentation control with a clear ownership boundary is a fresh, memorable interaction model with broad accessibility potential.
creativity_evidence: Guiding principle: website owns facts/functionality; user owns experience.
Cookie-persisted personal display experience.
usability_note: Natural-language preference setting can reduce technical barriers, though accessibility outcomes are not directly observable here.
red_flags: No video transcript; frame evidence could not be inspected.
standouts: Strong separation of content truth and presentation preference.
Concrete accessibility and cognitive-load use cases.
advance_reason: High-impact personalization layer with strong concept clarity and meaningful WebMCP delta.

one_line: Public coordination layer for agents to form teams, sign terms, verify work, recover from failure, and earn reputation.
what_it_does: Publishes missions, forms parties, freezes an immutable pact, streams ordered events, verifies hash-addressed work or PRs, replaces failed helpers, and issues signed receipts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP provides a typed browser-native front door into a public, shared coordination state; this is central to reliable agent collaboration rather than a UI convenience.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows Chrome discovering guild.list_missions directly through WebMCP with structured output.
A2A collaboration, signed pact, public events, and receipts extend the shared agent state beyond one UI.
execution_rationale: The video transcript demonstrates discovery, stale-evidence failure, repair, verification, and signed reputation receipt in a coherent protocol flow.
execution_evidence: 118-second video explicitly reports completed tool call, locked reward on stale head, update, verification pass, and receipt.
Public repo and alive demo reported.
impact_rationale: Multi-agent work has real coordination, trust, credential-sharing, and accountability problems; a public verifiable collaboration layer addresses them directly.
impact_evidence: Immutable pact fixes scope, work split, verification, failure rules, and reward.
Failure replacement preserves the original agreement and event history.
creativity_rationale: The guild metaphor is an effective presentation layer for a genuinely ambitious protocol combining WebMCP, MCP, A2A, signed terms, recovery, and reputation.
creativity_evidence: Fantasy guild is explicitly backed by real protocol evidence rather than simulation.
Dependable collaborators and recoverable failures are distinctive interaction concepts.
usability_note: Public mission board and visible event stream make complex coordination legible, though operational breadth may add complexity.
standouts: Failure recovery and signed receipts are demonstrated, not merely claimed.
advance_reason: Highly ambitious and well-evidenced agent collaboration infrastructure.

one_line: Deterministic front door that routes known fleet requests without models and sends novel requests to Gemini.
what_it_does: Uses pure-code guardrails and circuits for known capabilities, escalating only unmatched requests; reports a measured 180-of-200 circuit split and asynchronous job handling.
leverage_rationale: Structured routing and deterministic capability execution materially improve reliability, latency, and cost for a fleet, although the central optimization can exist outside WebMCP.
leverage_evidence: Description states known requests receive zero model calls and novel requests use Gemini explicitly.
Claims live Cloud Run measurement: 10 calls instead of 200 and ~100ms job-id handoff.
execution_rationale: The architecture and metrics are specific, but no video or frame sheets were submitted and the packet does not show the central workflow end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Public repo and alive demo reported.
Description gives a 200-request asynchronous batch and circuit/model paths.
impact_rationale: Reducing unnecessary model calls can improve cost, latency, determinism, and resilience for operators of large agent fleets; the problem is concrete.
impact_evidence: 21-agent fleet and 95% reduction claim.
Known procedures are identified as wasteful targets for deterministic handling.
creativity_rationale: A deterministic pre-model front door is a strong engineering angle on agent orchestration, though the routing pattern is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Moves model use to cases where it earns its cost.
Explicit zero-call circuit versus escalation split.
usability_note: Asynchronous job IDs and explicit routing are operationally sensible, but direct UI evidence is thin.
red_flags: Key performance claims are described but not independently demonstrated in the packet.
advance_reason: Useful infrastructure concept, but evidence is too thin for advancement in this packet.

one_line: Address-first Danish property and infrastructure explorer exposed to browser agents through WebMCP.
what_it_does: Resolves addresses and retrieves property, parcel, utility, environmental, map-layer, and source information while keeping the person in the same visible profile.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP turns fragmented public-data exploration into structured, address-scoped retrieval and synchronized navigation; a general agent would face substantial portal and dataset friction.
leverage_evidence: Tools resolve/verify addresses, retrieve property and utility context, screen environment, surface sources, and navigate visible sections.
Agent and person inspect the same address profile and original sources.
execution_rationale: The address-first workflow and public data sources are coherent, with public repo and alive demo; no video transcript and limited packet detail constrain end-to-end confidence.
execution_evidence: Built with Next.js, React, TypeScript and Danish public sources including Dataforsyningen.
Frame sheets and screenshot are listed, but could not be inspected.
impact_rationale: Homeowners, contractors, and advisers have a concrete burden navigating fragmented Danish property and utility data; one-address discovery is a credible simplification.
impact_evidence: Specific audiences and data domains are named.
Keeps source links available when exact authority records are needed.
creativity_rationale: Address-first aggregation of fragmented civic infrastructure data with shared agent/person evidence is a useful and somewhat original application.
creativity_evidence: User needs to know the address, not the bureaucracy or dataset behind it.
Language switching preserves Denmark as active data country.
usability_note: Address-first profile and source surfacing imply a clear workflow; visual verification was unavailable.
red_flags: About text says the application already existed before the challenge as unfinished, so origin is pre-existing.
Frame sheets could not be inspected.
standouts: Useful bridge between agent retrieval and authoritative public sources.
advance_reason: Credible civic-data product with strong audience fit and meaningful structured-agent advantage.
